title: Zero-helium wafer cooling with low-pressure hydrogen backside gas
idea: Ideal: etch/deposition chucks that need no helium. Closest achievable: run electrostatic-chuck backside cooling on 5-15 Torr H2 (thermal conductivity 0.18 vs 0.15 W/m-K for He) from on-site PEM electrolysis, with flow-limiting orifices and an N2-purged plenum so any leak stays below the flammability limit after exhaust dilution.
why: Helium: Qatar ~30% of supply offline since March 2026; backside cooling and purge are the dominant fab He uses. Removes ~60-80% of fab helium demand at equal heat transfer, using U.S.-made hydrogen.

title: Gasless chuck: solid-contact thermal coupling replaces backside gas
idea: Ideal: wafer cooling with no gas at all. Closest: an electrostatic chuck whose surface is a dense field of compliant micro-pillars capped with AlN/graphite composite; Johnsen-Rahbek clamping presses the wafer into intimate solid contact (>1000 W/m2K), and a replaceable pillar film handles wear.
why: Eliminates helium from chuck cooling plus He leak-check/recovery hardware; drives fab helium exposure for etch/CVD toward zero with roughly flat tool cost.

title: Crucible-free 300 mm silicon via cold-crucible induction skull melting
idea: Ideal: a crystal grown from a melt that touches nothing. Closest: pull 300 mm Cz crystals from a water-cooled segmented copper cold crucible where induction heats and partly levitates the melt and a frozen silicon skull is the container; interstitial oxygen for gettering is dosed via a controlled O2/Ar ambient instead of dissolving quartz.
why: Removes the Spruce Pine (>80%) high-purity quartz crucible chokepoint and gives tighter oxygen control; costs ~1.5-2x melt energy.

title: Turn polysilicon-plant waste SiCl4 into synthetic-silica crucibles
idea: Ideal: crucibles made from something we throw away. Closest: route silicon tetrachloride byproduct from U.S. Siemens-process polysilicon plants through flame hydrolysis into synthetic fused-silica soot, then sinter into full-body or inner-wall crucibles with ~10x lower metal impurities than natural HPQ.
why: Swaps the Spruce Pine HPQ chokepoint for a domestic waste stream (~3 t SiCl4 per t of poly already exists) and closes the chlorine loop.

title: Reusable mother wafer: grow, use, and peel thin epi films
idea: Ideal: a wafer that is never consumed. Closest: grow a 10-20 um epitaxial device layer on a porous-silicon double layer of a premium Cz mother wafer, build the DRAM, bond it to a cheap reclaimed/metallurgical-grade carrier, cleave at the porous layer, re-polish and reuse the mother 10-20 times.
why: Cuts Cz crystal growth, HPQ crucibles, polysilicon and puller energy per wafer ~10x; de-risks concentrated wafer supply chains.

title: Kerfless laser-split wafering of DRAM-grade silicon ingots
idea: Ideal: slicing with zero sawdust. Closest: focus an IR picosecond laser inside the ingot to write a sub-surface modified plane (KABRA-style, proven on SiC), then split each wafer off by thermal/ultrasonic stress; kerf drops from ~150 um to ~20 um and lapping shrinks.
why: ~30-40% more wafers per ingot, cutting polysilicon, quartz crucibles, puller energy, slurry and water per wafer proportionally.

title: Short local wordlines so abundant TiN replaces tungsten fill
idea: Ideal: a wordline with zero resistance. Work backward: make resistance irrelevant by splitting each buried wordline into 64-cell segments driven by local sub-wordline drivers placed under the array (CMOS-under-array), so all-TiN or doped-poly gates suffice and WF6 tungsten fill disappears.
why: Tungsten ~80% China, WF6 also consumes fluorine; segment RC falls ~16-64x (L squared), tolerating a 5-10x more resistive abundant conductor for ~3-5% driver area under the array.

title: Hafnium-, zirconium-, ruthenium-free CaTiO3 capacitors on MoO2 electrodes
idea: Ideal: a capacitor made from limestone and common metals. Closest: ALD perovskite CaTiO3 (bulk k~170) or Al-doped rutile TiO2 grown on a rutile-structured MoO2 bottom electrode that templates the high-k phase at <=400 C, replacing RuO2/Ru electrodes and ZrO2/HfO2 stacks.
why: Fact 1 asks for k~70: k>=80 could cut required capacitor AR from ~70 to ~40 while removing Zr/Hf (zircon byproducts) and Ru (South Africa ~90%); leakage is the open risk.

title: Fluorocarbon-free capacitor-hole etch by cryogenic HF/water vapor
idea: Ideal: high-aspect-ratio etch with no PFAS gases. Closest: etch 60-75:1 capacitor holes at -60 to -80 C using HF + H2O/NH4F chemistry where a condensed adsorbed HF layer drives ion-assisted SiO2 removal and frozen reaction products passivate sidewalls, dropping C4F6/C4F8/CH2F2 entirely.
why: Removes PFAS-classified, high-GWP fluorocarbon etch gases ahead of EU/US PFAS restrictions; reported ~2x faster cryo etch rates also cut etch-tool capex per wafer.

title: Two-phase CO2 chuck cooling replaces perfluorinated heat-transfer fluids
idea: Ideal: chillers with no exotic fluids. Closest: cool cryogenic etch chucks and chamber walls with pumped two-phase CO2 (R744) evaporating inside chuck channels (-50 C reachable), replacing Galden/Novec perfluoropolyether coolants after 3M's Novec exit.
why: Eliminates a PFAS supply chokepoint in every etch/deposition chiller; CO2 latent heat improves chuck temperature uniformity; GWP ~10,000 -> 1.

title: Vapor-deposited zinc-imidazolate MOF dry resist without fluorinated photoacids
idea: Ideal: a resist made from zinc and a common organic, deposited like a gas. Closest: grow ZIF-8-type zinc 2-methylimidazolate films by vapor-phase MOF-CVD; exposure breaks Zn-N links and the image develops in mild solvent or vapor, with no PFAS photoacid generators, fluorinated surfactants or spin-coat waste.
why: Resist PAGs/surfactants are a top fab PFAS use; dry deposition also cuts resist consumption ~10x and solvent wastewater; zinc is abundant.

title: Ceria-free planarization using UV-photocatalytic titania polishing pads
idea: Ideal: polishing with light instead of rare earths. Closest: embed anatase TiO2 in the CMP pad and illuminate through a transparent platen; photogenerated holes oxidize and soften Si/SiN/oxide surfaces so a dilute colloidal-silica slurry removes them, replacing CeO2 slurries in STI and ILD steps.
why: Semiconductor ceria is mostly Chinese rare-earth supply; also cuts slurry volume and wastewater across DRAM's dozens of CMP steps.

title: Supercritical-CO2 cleaning replaces most ultrapure-water wet cleans
idea: Ideal: a fab with no water. Closest: replace post-etch residue removal, post-CMP clean and capacitor-hole cleans with supercritical CO2 plus small co-solvent/chelator doses, which penetrates 100:1 holes with zero surface tension and is >95% recycled by depressurize-recompress loops.
why: DRAM fabs use ~10-20 M gal/day UPW; moving ~40% of cleans to scCO2 cuts water/wastewater proportionally and removes capillary collapse of tall capacitors (yield gain).

title: Sand-battery thermal storage time-shifts fab furnaces to cheap solar
idea: Ideal: a fab powered by free sunshine. Closest: charge a resistively heated sand/firebrick thermal store (600-1000 C) with midday solar surplus, use it to preheat furnace, epi and abatement gases and drive absorption chillers overnight, and schedule flexible batch steps (diffusion, anneal, reclaim) into low-price hours.
why: Thermal loads are ~30-40% of fab energy; time-shifting can cut energy cost 20-30% and peak grid capacity, easing U.S. fab siting.

title: Germanium-free 3D DRAM stacks using boron-doped silicon sacrificial layers
idea: Ideal: 3D tiers grown from silicon alone. Closest: grow the multi-tier epitaxial stack as alternating undoped Si and heavily boron-doped Si (or Si:C) instead of Si/SiGe, and remove sacrificial layers laterally by dopant-selective electrochemical porosification + oxidation or doping-selective wet etch.
why: Germanium (China ~60%+, export-controlled since 2023) is the default 3D DRAM sacrificial layer; Si/Si:B also removes lattice mismatch, allowing >100 tiers without relaxation defects (Fact 2).

title: Indium- and gallium-free zinc oxynitride channels for gain cells
idea: Ideal: an oxide transistor built only from zinc, oxygen and nitrogen. Closest: sputtered or ALD amorphous ZnON (mobility 50-100 cm2/Vs) stabilized with a few % Si or Al to suppress anion vacancies, replacing IGZO in 2T0C and 3D gain cells while keeping wide-gap ultra-low off-current.
why: Removes China-concentrated indium and export-controlled gallium from the lead capacitor-less candidate; higher mobility than IGZO (~10-20) gives faster writes.

title: Gold-free, glass-cloth-free DRAM packaging via fan-out redistribution
idea: Ideal: a package that is just the chip. Closest: replace board-on-chip gold-wire FBGA packages on BT laminate (near-monopoly T-glass cloth) with wafer-level fan-out: copper RDL plated directly over a reconstituted mold wafer, solder balls on the RDL.
why: Removes gold wire and BT/T-glass substrate chokepoints, shortens I/O paths (lower pJ/bit), ~20-30% lower package cost per GB.

title: Vacuum-gap storage capacitors with no dielectric material at all
idea: Ideal: a dielectric that costs nothing and never leaks. Closest: interdigitated vertical fin electrodes (TiN or doped Si) separated by a 4-6 nm sacrificial carbon layer that is ashed out through vent holes, leaving vacuum gaps held open by periodic oxide anchors; many fins in parallel recover capacitance.
why: Removes Hf/Zr high-k ALD and dielectric leakage (a refresh driver; vacuum tunneling at 1 V/5 nm is negligible); needs ~10x electrode area, so best for gain-cell/low-Cs designs.

title: One-metal cell: aluminum conductors with anodized-alumina dielectrics
idea: Ideal: one cheap material does everything. Closest: deposit a single aluminum film and convert chosen regions into dense barrier-type Al2O3 by room-temperature electrochemical anodization through a soft mask (thickness set at ~1.3 nm/V), so the same film supplies wordlines, plate electrodes and capacitor/gate dielectric.
why: Replaces W, TiN, Hf/Zr ALD and several vacuum steps with U.S.-abundant aluminum and wet benches; suits low-temperature oxide-TFT tiers; k~9 gives modest Cs but zero scarce inputs.

title: Self-rolling nanomembrane capacitors replace high-aspect-ratio etching
idea: Ideal: a capacitor that builds its own height. Closest: deposit a strained SiN bilayer carrying a TiN/Al2O3/TiN stack, release a sacrificial layer, and let built-in strain roll it into a 5-10-turn micro-scroll that multiplies electrode area per footprint 20-50x with no 70:1 hole etch.
why: Attacks the capacitor charge wall (Fact 1) without HAR etch (fluorocarbon gases, etch capex) or a k~70 material.

title: Refresh-free silicon-carbide DRAM in existing U.S. SiC power fabs
idea: Ideal: memory that never refreshes, made of silicon and carbon. Closest: 4H-SiC 1T1C cells (3.26 eV gap, generation leakage ~1e-19 of Si; 1990s demos showed multi-year room-temperature retention) built on 200 mm SiC lines in North Carolina/New York idled by the power-SiC glut.
why: Removes refresh (16-33% of idle power, 10-20% of bandwidth, Fact 3) using only Si, C and common dopants and idle U.S. capacity; density lags (larger F), so targets always-on low-power tiers.

title: Closed-loop recovery of tungsten, hafnium, zirconium from fab waste
idea: Ideal: scarce metals that never leave the fab. Closest: cold-trap and scrub unreacted WF6 and Zr/Hf amide precursors from ALD/CVD exhaust (ALD utilization is often <5%), chemically strip PVD shields and chamber kits, and ship recovered oxides to a domestic refiner for re-precursor synthesis.
why: Cuts net virgin W/Hf/Zr demand 50-80% and turns each fab into a domestic secondary mine against China W (~80%) and concentrated zircon supply.

title: Scarce-input substitution credits verified by digital material passports
idea: Ideal: a market that rewards memory made from nothing scarce. Closest: a U.S. per-GB production credit scaled by the share of the bill of materials free of designated chokepoints (helium, natural HPQ, Chinese-origin W/Ge/Ga/In, PFAS), verified with lot-level material passports (supplier attestations plus isotopic/trace fingerprints).
why: Creates demand pull for He-, W-, HPQ- and PFAS-free processes, pulling their time-to-volume in by years and shifting adoption risk from fabs to policy.

title: Gen-10.5 display-glass panels stacked with twenty tiers of oxide-TFT DRAM
idea: Ideal: memory sold like window glass. Closest: use Gen-10.5 display lines (~9.9 m2 panels) to build 2T0C/1T1C tiers from In-free ZnSnO TFTs, Mo/Al lines and planar Al2O3/TiO2 caps (TFT off-current ~1e-21 A/um makes small caps adequate), 4-5 masks per tier with panel nanoimprint at F~0.25 um, 20 tiers stacked at <=350 C.
why: 100x: panel processing ~$25/m2 per tier vs ~$150k/m2 for leading DRAM wafers; at ~0.5 um2/bit (~250 GB/m2/tier) x 20 tiers = 5 TB/m2 for ~$500 -> ~$0.1/GB vs ~$10/GB today. Trades latency (100-300 ns), volume and power; zero EUV, W, Hf, He.

title: Wound-film memory: roll-to-roll TFT DRAM coiled like a film capacitor
idea: Ideal: memory sold by the meter. Closest: imprint and print oxide-TFT DRAM arrays on 10 um aluminum/polyimide web at ~10 m/min, wind the web into a cylinder like a metallized-film capacitor, and connect every turn's wordline/bitline buses at the web edges via flame-sprayed 'schoopage' end metallization plus laser-cut edge decoders into parallel banks.
why: 100x: R2R processing ~$2-10/m2; a 1 m x 1000 m roll at 50-100 GB/m2 holds 50-100 TB for ~$10k -> ~$0.1-0.2/GB. Trades volume (a can-sized multi-TB brick), latency and thermal limits.

title: Anodic-alumina self-ordered pores replace lithography for vertical-channel stacks
idea: Ideal: a memory array that grows itself in a beaker. Closest: atop a Mo/SiO2 tier stack, anodize a Masuda-pre-textured aluminum film into perfectly ordered hexagonal pores (~40 nm pitch) used as a litho-free, self-aligned mask for the vertical holes; ALD ZnSnO channels make strings of 64-128 volatile gain cells, with bitlines registered to the AAO lattice rows.
why: 100x: array cell definition costs one wet anodization (~$0.1/m2) instead of EUV multipatterning; ~7e10 sites/cm2 x 100 tiers ~ 0.9 TB/cm2 raw, so even 5% array efficiency reaches ~$0.05-0.1/GB. Trades pore-domain defects (spare mapping) and us-class string latency hidden by caching.

title: Langmuir-assembled silica-sphere monolayers replace array lithography masks
idea: Ideal: a mask that assembles itself on water. Closest: self-assemble a close-packed monolayer of 40-60 nm Stober silica spheres on a Langmuir trough, transfer it to wafer or panel, shrink the spheres by O2/ion trimming, and use it as a hexagonal hard mask for capacitor-node or vertical-channel arrays; only coarse periphery uses conventional litho.
why: 100x: hexagonal DRAM arrays match a sphere lattice, so a cent of TEOS-derived spheres replaces an EUV exposure; with cheap multi-tier stacks array patterning cost per GB drops >100x. Trades grain-boundary defects needing spare rows and defect-tolerant mapping.

title: Commodity-plastic block copolymer DSA with infiltration-grown alumina hard masks
idea: Ideal: patterns written by molecules for free. Closest: spin high-chi PS-b-P2VP that self-assembles into 16-24 nm-pitch hexagonal cylinders, use sequential infiltration synthesis (TMA/H2O) to grow AlOx inside one block as an etch-robust inorganic mask, and guide it with cheap ArF-dry or imprint patterns at 4-6x pitch.
why: 100x: removes all 5-7 EUV layers from the array (per-layer patterning cost down ~20-50x) and, stacked over many cheap tiers, supports ~$0.1/GB; trades defectivity (need ~1/cm2) and anneal time.

title: Embrace random wiring: self-assembled crossbars mapped after fabrication
idea: Ideal: wiring that costs nothing because nobody designs it. Closest: grow dense random or partly ordered nanoline crossbars (dewetting, DSA) with a cell wherever lines cross; reach lines through a coarse-litho stochastic decoder (randomly doped address wires, Lieber/DeHon style) and run a one-time BIST discovery pass that writes a per-chip address-translation table.
why: 100x: shifts cost from lithographic precision to cheap logic and test time; if 30-50% of random cells are usable, $/GB falls ~100x versus precision-patterned arrays. Trades ~1-3% map overhead and variable capacity per die.

title: Redox-molecule monolayers store several-fold more charge in planar capacitors
idea: Ideal: a capacitor where every molecule holds electrons. Closest: self-assemble multi-state redox molecules (porphyrin/ferrocene tripods with phosphonate anchors, ZettaCore-style) on a TiN or doped-oxide electrode with an ionic-gel counter electrode; ~1e14 molecules/cm2 x 1-2 electrons gives ~16-32 uC/cm2 vs ~5-7 for a 1 V planar ZrO2 cap.
why: 100x enabler: lets cheap planar cells on panels/legacy fabs hold enough charge, collapsing the capacitor module (HAR etch, Zr/Hf ALD, several masks) into one dip-coat on the path to ~$0.1/GB. Trades molecule stability (needs >1e15 cycles) and redox speed.

title: Volatile 3D NAND: direct-tunnel charge-trap strings run as DRAM
idea: Ideal: DRAM at flash prices. Closest: build a 200+-layer 3D-NAND-style string with a 1.5-2.0 nm tunnel oxide (vs 5-7 nm) so programming is direct tunneling at ~4-6 V in ~100 ns without Fowler-Nordheim damage, giving ~1e12+ endurance; retention falls to ~1-10 s, so the array is refreshed like DRAM behind a DRAM-cache controller.
why: 100x: inherits 3D NAND's ~$0.05/GB cost structure and Si/N/O/Mo materials, ~100-200x below current DRAM pricing; trades us-class string read latency (hidden by a front cache), refresh power and an unproven endurance case.

title: Vertical charge-coupled shift strings: memory without per-bit transistors
idea: Ideal: memory with no transistor, capacitor or contact per bit. Closest: in a 3D-NAND-like stack, clock tier wordlines three-phase so charge packets move along a vertical oxide-semiconductor channel like a CCD; each string is a shift register read by one sense amp at its foot, with a regeneration stage every ~32 tiers to cancel transfer loss.
why: 100x: deletes the cell capacitor, contacts and leakage tail (Facts 1-3), uses only Si/O/N/Mo, and scales density with tier count at ~3D-NAND cost (~$0.05/GB). Trades serial access (~100-300 ns per 64-stage shift, hidden by bank interleaving) and charge-transfer efficiency.

title: Ion-beam ripple self-patterning writes wafer-wide nanoline arrays without masks
idea: Ideal: line arrays that appear by themselves under a flood beam. Closest: off-normal low-energy Ar+ sputtering of an a-Si or metal hard-mask film spontaneously forms Bradley-Harper ripples at 20-40 nm wavelength, phase-locked by a coarse pre-pattern; transfer them as wordline/bitline gratings and repeat rotated 90 degrees for the crossing grid.
why: 100x: pattern formation costs one broad-beam ion-source step (tens of $k tooling) instead of SAQP/EUV, cutting array patterning per layer >50x and enabling ~$0.1/GB in multi-tier stacks; trades long-range order and line-edge roughness.

title: Square-meter laser interference lithography for perfectly periodic memory arrays
idea: Ideal: one flash of light patterns a whole panel. Closest: two- or three-beam interference of a 266/213 nm solid-state laser writes periodic lines or hexagonal dots (pitch >=0.12 um) over Gen-8 panels or R2R webs in seconds with no reticle or projection optics; only periphery and staircases use cheap panel steppers.
why: 100x: memory arrays are periodic, so they need no imaging optics; tool capex per m2 is ~1000x below EUV, enabling the ~0.25 um-F panel/foil tiers needed for ~$0.1/GB. Trades 5-10x larger F and stitching/overlay risk.

title: Directionally solidified eutectic films freeze into aligned nanoscale wordline lamellae
idea: Ideal: wires that freeze into place. Closest: laser zone-melt a thin film of an abundant eutectic (Al-Al2Cu or NiAl-Mo) on an insulating substrate so directional solidification grows aligned conducting lamellae at 30-80 nm spacing set by scan speed (lambda^2 v = const); selectively etch one phase to leave parallel metal lines.
why: 100x: line patterning becomes a cents-per-m2 thermal process; combined with cheap tiered substrates it targets >=100x lower $/GB with abundant Al/Cu/Ni/Mo (no W). Trades lamellar faults (sparing) and period tolerance.

title: Vacuum-free tier stacks grown by pulsed-electrodeposition superlattices
idea: Ideal: a 3D memory stack poured from a bath. Closest: pulse-electroplate 100+ periods of Ni or Cu conductor layers alternating with cathodically deposited ZnO semiconductor/dielectric layers (~20-40 nm each, <90 C, aqueous) to replace CVD/PVD tier depositions for 3D gain-cell stacks.
why: 100x path: plating tools ~$1-3M vs $10-30M vacuum clusters, no helium or vacuum pumps, abundant Zn/Ni/Cu; tier cost falls ~10-30x, which with self-patterned holes targets ~$0.1/GB. Trades film quality and interface traps (more refresh).

title: S-layer protein crystals template ten-nanometer charge-storage dot arrays
idea: Ideal: a nanopattern brewed in a fermenter. Closest: recrystallize bacterial S-layer proteins (2D lattices, 3-30 nm period, cheap fermentation) on a gate dielectric, use their pores to template ALD/electroless Ni or ZnO nanodots as isolated charge sites for a dense floating-dot volatile cell, then burn the protein away.
why: 100x: protein at ~$1/g covers ~1e4 m2 per gram; sub-15 nm periodic sites without litho enable dense multi-level cells on cheap tiers toward ~$0.1/GB. Trades thermal limits and domain defects.

title: All-oxide CMOS periphery lets memory panels need no silicon chips
idea: Ideal: periphery made from the same cheap film as the cells. Closest: build sense amps, decoders and refresh logic from complementary oxide TFTs (n-ZnSnO with p-SnO or p-Cu2O, all abundant, <=300 C) using bootstrapped dynamic logic to compensate the weak p-FET, so panel memory needs no bonded silicon driver ICs.
why: 100x enabler: periphery is ~49% of DRAM die (Fact 7); moving it onto ~$30/m2 panel layers is required to reach ~$0.1/GB. Trades sensing speed (50-200 ns) and power.

title: Atmospheric spatial ALD on moving webs: no vacuum, no helium
idea: Ideal: atomic-precision films made in open air. Closest: spatial-ALD heads with gas-bearing-separated precursor zones (TMA/H2O, DEZ/H2O, TiCl4/H2O) coat 1-2 m webs or panels at 1-5 m/min at atmospheric pressure, laying down gate oxide, capacitor dielectric and ZnO channel with no vacuum chambers, He backside cooling or PFAS chamber cleans.
why: 100x path: deposition is ~20-25% of fab capex and spatial-ALD tool cost per m2/hr is ~100x below cluster ALD, a pillar of ~$0.1/GB panel/foil memory. Trades film density and dielectric leakage (more refresh).

title: Contamination-tolerant oxide memory built in warehouse-grade cleanrooms
idea: Ideal: memory that can be built in a garage. Closest: pick cell materials (wide-gap oxide channels, Al2O3, Mo) whose leakage is insensitive to Fe/Cu/Na at 10-100x semiconductor limits, and run them in ISO-6 sealed-minienvironment 'warehouse fabs' with display/solar-grade chemicals and gases costing ~5-10x less than ppt-grade.
why: 100x path: cleanroom, UPW and ultra-pure chemicals are ~30-40% of fab capex/opex; removing them, stacked on cheap-substrate tiers, cuts the cost stack toward 100x per GB and speeds U.S. buildout. Trades yield-learning risk and leakage margin.

title: Retired-server DIMM reclamation business delivering tens-of-cents-per-GB pooled memory
idea: Ideal: memory that already exists and costs nothing. Closest: buy decommissioned DDR4/DDR5 DIMMs from hyperscaler refresh cycles at scrap-plus prices, auto-test and grade them, and mount them on CXL Type-3 expander cards whose controllers remap weak rows and add stronger ECC, sold as pooled second-tier memory.
why: 100x: many PB retire each year; marginal cost is test + card + controller (~$0.05-0.15/GB at scale), ~50-100x below new-DRAM pricing, with zero new wafers, helium or tungsten. Trades +70-150 ns CXL latency, power and supply variability.

title: Self-assembled nanopillar composites multiply capacitor area in one deposition
idea: Ideal: an electrode that sprouts its own forest. Closest: co-sputter a phase-separating film (conductive TiN or NiO-type pillars in an Al2O3/MgO matrix) that spontaneously forms ~5 nm vertical pillars at ~10 nm spacing, etch back the matrix and coat with ALD dielectric and top electrode for 10-30x area gain with no patterning or HAR etch.
why: 100x enabler: gives cheap planar/panel cells pillar-class capacitance for ~$1/m2, deleting capacitor-module masks and fluorocarbon HAR etch on the ~$0.1/GB path. Trades pillar uniformity and tip leakage.

title: Metal-assisted chemical etching grows vertical channel forests at room temperature
idea: Ideal: sculpting deep silicon with no plasma. Closest: dewet a thin Ag film (or deposit Ag through a self-assembled mask) on silicon; in HF/H2O2 at room temperature the silver sinks vertically, leaving 100:1 nanopillars at 30-60 nm pitch for vertical-channel transistors or capacitor cores, made on plastic wet benches instead of $20M+ C4F6-burning etchers.
why: 100x path: wet-bench cost per wafer-pass is ~1-5% of a HAR plasma etch and removes PFAS etch gases; with self-assembled masks, array formation cost per GB falls >=100x. Trades pillar wander, Ag contamination control and porosity.

title: Self-replicating nanoimprint stamps make each memory layer cost cents
idea: Ideal: a mask that copies itself forever. Closest: write one e-beam quartz master per layer, replicate it into thousands of UV-cured polymer daughter stamps (and granddaughters from those), and use each daughter for ~100 roll-to-plate imprints on panels or wafers before recycling.
why: 100x: litho (5-7 EUV layers, depreciation ~55% of wafer cost, Fact 4) dominates; mask+exposure cost per layer goes from ~$0.5-1 per die-area-equivalent to <$0.01. Trades overlay (~10-20 nm) and defect accumulation across stamp generations (spare rows).

title: Spacer cascade turns solar-grade screen printing into nanoscale lines
idea: Ideal: nanolines from the cheapest printing tool on Earth. Closest: screen- or gravure-print 10-20 um mandrel lines on panels or wafers, then run eight successive conformal-deposition/etch-back spacer cycles (each doubling line count, 2^8 = 256x) to reach ~50-80 nm-pitch gratings using only blanket depositions and etches.
why: 100x: swaps EUV/ArF capex for blanket steps costing ~$0.1-0.5/m2 each, cutting array patterning for panel memory >100x. Trades CD variation accumulated over cycles and supports only regular gratings.

title: Thermally drawn preform ribbons shrink centimeter laminates into nanoscale cells
idea: Ideal: draw memory like optical fiber, kilometers at a time. Closest: stack a cm-scale preform of glass, oxide semiconductor and low-melting metal (Sn-Zn or Al alloy) laminates in a cell cross-section, thermally draw it 1000-10,000x into ribbons whose layers shrink to 10-50 nm, then cut and tile ribbons orthogonally into crossbar or gain-cell tiers.
why: 100x: draw towers produce km/hour at ~$0.01/m and define features by geometric draw-down, not lithography; a speculative >=100x $/GB path from abundant glass, oxide and metal. Trades interlayer diffusion during draw, coarse tiling contacts and unproven semiconductor quality.
